title: Kashmir, 1819
hookLine: the valley comes under Sikh rule

lines: A VALLEY RULED FROM FAR AWAY.
cards: Snow on the passes. A lake with houseboats. Fields of saffron, and shawls so fine, the old stories say, that one could be drawn through a ring.
That's Kashmir, the valley ringed by mountains north of the Punjab. For a long time it had been ruled from far away, by governors sent from Kabul.
Then, as Sikh histories tell it, an army came up the mountain roads from Lahore, dragging its guns behind it.

teach.h: A HARD ROAD OVER THE PASSES.
teach.b: Start with the road. Getting an army into Kashmir meant hauling men and guns over high passes, and Sikh histories remember that an earlier try had failed. So the second was planned with care.

The Maharaja sent his general, Misr Diwan Chand, a Hindu officer who had risen in his service, with Sikh commanders beside him. The army crossed the mountains, met the Afghan governor's forces, and won the valley.
Then the change at the top.

Kashmir had been held for the kings in Kabul; now its governors were named in Lahore. Histories tell of Kashmir's shawls and saffron reaching the Lahore court, and of the Maharaja's love of fine Kashmiri things.
Ruling a valley is harder than winning one. Some governors sent from Lahore are remembered well, some less so, and Kashmiri memory of these years is mixed. That belongs in the story too.

teach.h: A WEEK OF A GROWING KINGDOM.
teach.b: And look back at this week: gold laid on the Harmandir, a river fixed as a border, an army trained by teachers from many lands, a general who held the frontier, a Maharaja who bowed to correction at the Akal Takht, Multan in the heat.
Day by day, a city became a country.
The valley is where the map reached the snow.

how: Sikhs meet the Kashmir campaign in histories of Maharaja Ranjit Singh's reign, where it is told as one of the conquests that took the kingdom into the mountains.

a river crossing on the old road to Kabul

games.q: you're the Maharaja. one army has already failed to cross the passes into Kashmir. what do you do?
o: send a trusted general with a carefully planned second try.
ask Kabul to hand it over.
games.why: he sent Misr Diwan Chand with Sikh commanders, and the second try won the valley.

practice: Picture mountains on every side of you, close and high, snow on their tops, and down where you sit, sheltered green ground and water moving somewhere nearby.
Breathe in the cold, clean air, breathe out slowly, and let the mountains hold the week's noise outside. If you pray, you can say Waheguru quietly on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Kashmir. The valley of snow, saffron and shawls, won by an army that crossed the passes from Lahore, and governed from there.

orig.note: Gurmukhi for Kashmir, the valley to the north of the Punjab.

carryVoice: Your line: the valley. Winning a place is easier than ruling it well. That's the week, done.
